(A.46)

From (A.39) we get #𝒱𝒢nε​ε(D)≤ε−1/2−ζ\#\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{n_{\varepsilon}\varepsilon}(D)\leq\varepsilon^{-1/2-\zeta}. By applying this and the upper bound in (A.35) to estimate the right side of (A.46), we obtain

∑x∈𝒱​𝒢ε​(D)f⁡(wxε)​degε⁡(x)\displaystyle\sum_{x\in\mathcal{V}\mathcal{G}^{\varepsilon}(D)}f(w_{x}^{\varepsilon})\operatorname{deg}^{\varepsilon}(x) OPEN≤6​ε−1​∫Df⁡(z)​d​μh​(z)+nεα0​ε−1+α0+Oε​(εq/2−1−β−ζCLOSE)\displaystyle\leq 6\varepsilon^{-1}\int_{D}f(z)\,d\mu_{h}(z)+n_{\varepsilon}^{\alpha_{0}}\varepsilon^{-1+\alpha_{0}}+O_{\varepsilon}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\varepsilon^{q/2-1-\beta-\zeta}}}\right)
OPEN≤6​ε−1​∫Df⁡(z)​d​μh​(z)+Oε​(ε−1+αCLOSE)\displaystyle\leq 6\varepsilon^{-1}\int_{D}f(z)\,d\mu_{h}(z)+O_{\varepsilon}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\varepsilon^{-1+\alpha}}}\right)

for any choice of α<min⁡{α0,q/2−β−ζ}\alpha<\min\{\alpha_{0},\,q/2-\beta-\zeta\}. If we choose ζ\zeta and β\beta sufficiently small, in a manner depending only on q,γq,\gamma, then we can arrange that this minimum is positive. Thus, after possibly slightly shrinking α\alpha we get that the upper bound in (A.21) holds for small enough ε>0\varepsilon>0.

We similarly obtain the lower bound in (A.21) using the lower bounds in each of (A.35) and (A.43). ∎

A.3 Space-filling SLE loops

Let κ>4\kappa>4, let D⊂ℂD\subset\mathbbm{C} be a simply connected domain, and let a∈∂Da\in\partial D be a prime end. The purpose of this section is to explain one possible definition of the counterclockwise space-filling SLE loop η\eta in DD based at aa, and to show that this space-filling SLE loop can be obtained as the limit (for a rather strong notion of convergence) of space-filling SLE from aa to bb in DD as b→ab\rightarrow a from the clockwise direction. The proofs in this section are based on the theory of imaginary geometry from [MS16a, MS16b, MS16c, MS17]. We will mostly focus on the case when (D,a)=(ℍ,∞)(D,a)=(\mathbbm{H},\infty); the space-filling SLE loop for other choices of (D,a)(D,a) will be defined via conformal mapping.

Fix κ>4\kappa>4. As in [MS16a, MS16b, MS16c, MS17], we define the constant

λ′:=πκ.\lambda^{\prime}:=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{\kappa}}. (A.47)

Note that our κ\kappa is called κ′\kappa^{\prime} in [MS16a, MS16b, MS16c, MS17].

Let hh be a zero-boundary GFF on ℍ\mathbbm{H} plus the constant −λ′-\lambda^{\prime}. For z∈ℚ2∩ℍz\in\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}, let ηz,L\eta^{z,L} (resp. ηz,R\eta^{z,R}) be the flow line of hh started from zz with angle π/2\pi/2 (resp. −π/2-\pi/2) and stopped at the first time it hits ℝ\mathbbm{R}, as defined in [MS17, Theorem 1.1]. The law of ηz,L\eta^{z,L} is locally absolutely continuous w.r.t. that of a SLE(16/κ−2)16/κ{}_{16/\kappa}(16/\kappa-2) curve in any interval of time before it hits ℝ\mathbbm{R}. By [MS17, Theorem 1.9], for distinct z,w∈ℚ2∩ℍz,w\in\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}, a.s. the curves ηz,L\eta^{z,L} and ηw,L\eta^{w,L} (resp. ηz,L\eta^{z,L} and ηw,R\eta^{w,R}) a.s. merge into each other after some finite time. We define a total order ⪯\preceq on ℚ2∩ℍ\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H} by declaring that z⪯wz\preceq w if and only if zz lies in a connected component of ℍ∖(ηw,L∪ηw,R)\mathbbm{H}\setminus(\eta^{w,L}\cup\eta^{w,R}) whose boundary is traced by the left side of ηw,L\eta^{w,L} and the right side of ηw,R\eta^{w,R}.

For a<0a<0, let ηa\eta_{a} be a chordal space-filling SLEκ from aa to ∞\infty. Let ⪯a\preceq_{a} be the total order on ℚ2∩ℍ\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H} induced by ηa\eta_{a}, i.e., z⪯awz\preceq_{a}w if and only if ηa\eta_{a} hits zz before ww. Due to the construction of space-filling SLEκ in [MS17, Section 1.2.3], the ordering ⪯a\preceq_{a} admits the following equivalent description. Let hah_{a} be a GFF on ℍ\mathbbm{H} with boundary data λ′\lambda^{\prime} on (−∞,a](-\infty,a] and −λ′-\lambda^{\prime} on [a,∞)[a,\infty). Then we can realize ηa\eta_{a} as the space-filling SLEκ counterflow line of hah_{a} from aa to ∞\infty. Furthermore, if we define the flow lines ηaz,L\eta_{a}^{z,L} and ηaz,R\eta_{a}^{z,R} for z∈ℚ2∩ℍz\in\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H} in the same manner as ηz,L\eta^{z,L} and ηz,R\eta^{z,R} above but with hah_{a} in place of hh, then for z∈ℚ2∩ℍz\in\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H} the curves ηaz,L\eta_{a}^{z,L} and ηaz,R\eta_{a}^{z,R} are the left and right outer boundaries of ηa\eta_{a} stopped at the first time it hits zz. We note that ηaz,L\eta_{a}^{z,L} (resp. ηaz,R\eta_{a}^{z,R}) stops upon hitting (−∞,a](-\infty,a] (resp. [a,∞)[a,\infty)). Consequently, the ordering ⪯a\preceq_{a} can be defined in the same manner as the ordering ⪯\preceq above but with hah_{a} in place of hh.

Proposition A.10.

There is a unique continuous curve η:ℝ→ℍ¯\eta:\mathbbm{R}\rightarrow\overline{\mathbbm{H}} from ∞\infty to ∞\infty which satisfies η⁡(0)=0\eta(0)=0 and area⁡η⁡([s,t])=t−s\operatorname{area}\eta([s,t])=t-s for each s<ts<t, hits the points of ℚ2∩ℍ\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H} in the order specified by ⪯\preceq, and fills in all of ℍ\mathbbm{H}. The law of η\eta is scale and translation invariant in the sense that for C>0C>0 and b∈ℝb\in\mathbbm{R}, we have C​η+b​=𝑑​ηC\eta+b\overset{d}{=}\eta viewed as curves modulo time parametrization. Moreover, for each fixed r>0r>0 it holds that ⪯a|Br​(0)∩ℚ2∩ℍ\preceq_{a}|_{B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}} converges to ⪯|Br​(0)∩ℚ2∩ℍ\preceq|_{B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}} in the total variation sense as a→−∞a\rightarrow-\infty.

Definition A.11.

The curve η\eta of Proposition A.10 is defined to be the counterclockwise space-filling SLEκ loop based at ∞\infty in ℍ\mathbbm{H}. The clockwise space-filling SLEκ loop based at ∞\infty in ℍ\mathbbm{H} is the curve η~\widetilde{\eta} which is the image of η\eta under the anticonformal map x+i​y↦−x+i​yx+iy\mapsto-x+iy. For a domain DD and a prime end b∈∂Db\in\partial D, we define the counterclockwise (resp. clockwise) space-filling SLEκ loop based at bb in DD to be the image of η\eta (resp. η~\widetilde{\eta}) under a conformal map ℍ→D\mathbbm{H}\rightarrow D which takes ∞\infty to bb, viewed as a curve modulo time parametrization (the law of this curve does not depend on the choice of conformal map due to the scale / translation invariance property of η\eta).

It is possible to establish the existence of the curve η\eta of Proposition A.10 by repeating essentially the same arguments used in [MS17] to construct space-filling SLE with distinct starting and ending points. However, in order to make our proof easier to follow and to get the total variation convergence statement, we will instead deduce Proposition A.10 from existing results in the literature. The key idea of the proof is that when aa is very negative, the restrictions of hh and hah_{a} to a fixed neighborhood of 0 in ℍ\mathbbm{H} are close in the total variation sense, and moreover the orderings ⪯\preceq and ⪯a\preceq_{a} are in a certain sense locally determined by hh and hah_{a}, respectively.

Let us now specify a precise version of the locality property of ⪯a\preceq_{a}. For a radius ρ>0\rho>0, let TaρT_{a}^{\rho} (resp. SaρS_{a}^{\rho}) be the first time that ηa\eta_{a} enters Bρ​(0)∩ℍB_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H} before hitting 00 (resp. the last time that ηa\eta_{a} enters Bρ​(0)∩ℍB_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H} after hitting 0). We define

ηaρ:=ηa|[Taρ,Saρ]andKaρ:=ηa​([Taρ,Saρ]).\eta_{a}^{\rho}:=\eta_{a}|_{[T_{a}^{\rho},S_{a}^{\rho}]}\quad\text{and}\quad K_{a}^{\rho}:=\eta_{a}([T_{a}^{\rho},S_{a}^{\rho}]). (A.48)

We now describe KaρK_{a}^{\rho} in terms of ⪯a\preceq_{a}.

Lemma A.12.

Let ηa0,L\eta_{a}^{0,L} be the flow line of hah_{a} started from 0 with angle π/2\pi/2. If z∈Bρ​(0)∩ℚ2∩ℍz\in B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}, then z∈Kaρz\in K_{a}^{\rho} if and only if ηaz,L\eta_{a}^{z,L} merges into ηa0,L\eta_{a}^{0,L} before leaving Bρ​(0)B_{\rho}(0) and ηaz,R\eta_{a}^{z,R} hits [a,∞)[a,\infty) before leaving Bρ​(0)B_{\rho}(0).

Proof.

This follows since ηaz,L\eta_{a}^{z,L} and ηaz,R\eta_{a}^{z,R} are the left/right outer boundaries of ηa\eta_{a} at the (a.s. unique) time when it hits aa and ηa0,L\eta_{a}^{0,L} is the outer boundary of ηa\eta_{a} at the (a.s. unique) time when it hits 0. ∎

As a consequence of Lemma A.12 and the fact that the flow lines ηaz,L\eta_{a}^{z,L} and ηaz,R\eta_{a}^{z,R} are locally determined by hh (c.f. the proof of [GMS19, Lemma 2.4]), it follows that ⪯a|Kaρ∩ℚ2\preceq_{a}|_{K_{a}^{\rho}\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}} is a.s. determined by ha|Bρ​(0)∩ℍh_{a}|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}.

Let η0,L\eta^{0,L} be the flow line of hh started from 0 with angle π/2\pi/2. Let KρK^{\rho} be the closure of the set of z∈Bρ​(0)∩ℚ2∩ℍz\in B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H} such that z∈Kaρz\in K_{a}^{\rho} if and only if ηz,L\eta^{z,L} merges into η0,L\eta^{0,L} before exiting Bρ​(0)B_{\rho}(0) and ηz,R\eta^{z,R} hits ℝ\mathbbm{R} before leaving Bρ​(0)B_{\rho}(0). That is, KρK^{\rho} is defined in the same way as KaρK_{a}^{\rho} but with hh in place of hah_{a}. By definition, KρK^{\rho} is a.s. determined by h|Bρ​(0)∩ℍh|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}.

A basic Radon-Nikodym estimate for the GFF (see, e.g., the proof of [MS16a, Proposition 3.4] shows that the following is true for each ρ>0\rho>0.

  • •

    If a<−ρa<-\rho, then the laws of ha|Bρ​(0)∩ℍh_{a}|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}} and h|Bρ​(0)∩ℍh|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}} are mutually absolutely continuous.

  • •

    The total variation distance between the laws of ha|Bρ​(0)∩ℍh_{a}|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}} and h|Bρ​(0)∩ℍh|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}} tends to zero as a→−∞a\rightarrow-\infty.

In particular,

OPENOPEN(Kaρ,⪯a|Kaρ∩ℚ2)→(Kρ,⪯|Kρ∩ℚ2)in total variation as a→−∞.\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(K_{a}^{\rho},\preceq_{a}|_{K_{a}^{\rho}\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}}}}\right)\rightarrow\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(K^{\rho},\preceq|_{K^{\rho}\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}}}}\right)\quad\text{in total variation as $a\rightarrow-\infty$}. (A.49)
Lemma A.13.

Let r>0r>0 and let p∈(0,1)p\in(0,1). There exists ρ=ρ⁡(r,p)>r\rho=\rho(r,p)>r such that

ℙ[Br(0)∩ℍ⊂Kρ]≥pand\mathbbm{P}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}\subset K^{\rho}}}\right]\geq p\quad\text{and} (A.50)
lim infa→−∞ℙ[Br(0)∩ℍ⊂Kaρ]≥p.\liminf_{a\rightarrow-\infty}\mathbbm{P}\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left[B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}\subset K_{a}^{\rho}}}\right]\geq p. (A.51)
Proof.

Due to the total variation convergence Kaρ→KρK_{a}^{\rho}\rightarrow K^{\rho}, it suffices to show that there exists ρ=ρ⁡(r,p)>r\rho=\rho(r,p)>r such that (A.50) holds. To prove this, we will first show that K1K^{1} contains some neighborhood of 0 with probability at least pp then use a scaling argument. Choose a0∈ℕa_{0}\in\mathbbm{N} with a0<−1a_{0}<-1. Since the laws of ha0|Bρ​(0)∩ℍh_{a_{0}}|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}} and h|Bρ​(0)∩ℍh|_{B_{\rho}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}} are mutually absolutely continuous, also the laws of Ka01K_{a_{0}}^{1} and K1K^{1} are mutually absolutely continuous. Since ηa0\eta_{a_{0}} is a chordal space-filling SLEκ, a.s. Ka01K_{a_{0}}^{1} contains some neighborhood of 0 in ℍ\mathbbm{H}. Hence for any q∈(0,1)q\in(0,1) there exists ε>0\varepsilon>0 such that ℙ[Bε(0)∩ℍ⊂ηa01]≥q\mathbbm{P}[B_{\varepsilon}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}\subset\eta_{a_{0}}^{1}]\geq q. By taking qq to be sufficiently close to 1 (depending on pp) we infer that there exists ε>0\varepsilon>0 such that

ℙ[Bε(0)∩ℍ⊂K1]≥p.\mathbbm{P}[B_{\varepsilon}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}\subset K^{1}]\geq p. (A.52)

Due to the scale invariance of the law of hh, we have ρ​K1​=𝑑​Kρ\rho K^{1}\overset{d}{=}K^{\rho} for each rational ρ>0\rho>0. Therefore (A.50) for ρ\rho a rational number slightly larger than r/εr/\varepsilon follows from (A.52). ∎

Proof of Proposition A.10.

Each ηa\eta_{a} is a continuous curve which satisfies the conditions of the proposition statement with hah_{a} in place of hh. Due to the total variation convergence (A.49), we infer that for each ρ>0\rho>0, there is a unique curve η¯ρ\overline{\eta}^{\rho} mapping some time interval [Tρ,Sρ][T^{\rho},S^{\rho}] into KρK^{\rho} which satisfies η⁡(0)=0\eta(0)=0 and area⁡η⁡([s,t])=t−s\operatorname{area}\eta([s,t])=t-s for each s<ts<t and such that η¯ρ\overline{\eta}^{\rho} hits the points of Kρ∩ℚ2K^{\rho}\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2} in the order specified by ⪯\preceq. By (A.50) of Lemma A.13 and since rr can be made arbitrarily large, it follows that the sets KρK^{\rho} a.s. increase to all of ℂ\mathbbm{C} as ρ→∞\rho\rightarrow\infty. In particular, a.s. Sρ→−∞S^{\rho}\rightarrow-\infty and Tρ→∞T^{\rho}\rightarrow\infty as ρ→∞\rho\rightarrow\infty. We therefore get a random continuous curve η\eta from −∞-\infty to ∞\infty which satisfies the conditions in the first assertion of the lemma.

Furthermore, by the scale and translation invariance of the law of hh we get that the law of the ordering ⪯\preceq is invariant under scaling by rational scaling factors and translation by rational elements of ℝ\mathbbm{R} (we need to restrict to rationals at this point since we defined our ordering using ℚ2\mathbbm{Q}^{2}). This shows that the law of η\eta, viewed modulo time parametrization, is invariant under rational scalings and translations.

By (A.51) of Lemma A.13 and (A.49), we get that ⪯a|Br​(0)∩ℚ2∩ℍ\preceq_{a}|_{B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}} converges to ⪯|Br​(0)∩ℚ2∩ℍ\preceq|_{B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap\mathbbm{H}} in the total variation sense as a→−∞a\rightarrow-\infty.

It remains to show that the law of η\eta, viewed modulo time parametrization, is in fact invariant under all scalings and translations, not just rational ones. To prove this, we observe that if C>0C>0, then the argument above works equally well with C​ℚ2C\mathbbm{Q}^{2} in place of ℚ2\mathbbm{Q}^{2}. Let ηC\eta^{C} be the curve obtained in the same way as η\eta but with C​ℚ2C\mathbbm{Q}^{2} in place of ℚ2\mathbbm{Q}^{2}. Then the law of ηC\eta^{C}, viewed modulo time parametrization, is invariant under scalings and translations by rational multiples of CC. On the other hand, replacing ℚ2\mathbbm{Q}^{2} by C​ℚ2C\mathbbm{Q}^{2} does not change the curves ηa\eta_{a}. From the total variation convergence ⪯aC|C​ℚ2∩Br​(0)∩ℍ→⪯C|C​ℚ2∩Br​(0)∩ℍ\preceq_{a}^{C}|_{C\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}}\rightarrow\preceq^{C}|_{C\mathbbm{Q}^{2}\cap B_{r}(0)\cap\mathbbm{H}} (in obvious notation) for each r>0r>0 we therefore get that ηC​=𝑑​η\eta^{C}\overset{d}{=}\eta. Since CC is arbitrary we now conclude the proof. ∎

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.
